data.narrative:
CubeFabs is a Series E semiconductor company founded by Matthew Putman (PhD, former Columbia materials science professor) and John Putman, having raised approximately $182M to date. The target operates within Chips & Semiconductors, a sector represented by 11 peer companies (3 public: ALAB, NVDA, AMD; 8 private including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent).

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The narrow peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables—only 1 adjacent-stage peer was identified against a minimum threshold of 3 datapoints needed for statistical relevance. An all-sector median approach would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of business models, technology maturity, and capital intensity across semiconductor subsectors.

Without triangulation via peer multiples, this valuation requires alternative methods not covered in the provided dataset (e.g., DCF analysis, precedent transaction analysis, or calibration to disclosed funding round pricing). The current analysis confirms that CubeFabs cannot be reliably valued using peer comps alone. A complete assessment would require either access to pricing data from the Series E round itself, detailed financial projections, or identification of transaction precedent in frontier semiconductor infrastructure funding.
